Header: Agrotis ipsilon Black cutworm, overflow worm, 小地老虎 in Chinese

Prevention: Delay sowing for 5-10 days in spring to escape cutworm occurrence.
Eliminate weeds to reduce adult moths laying eggs on weeds during growing season.
Flood 3h during seedling stage after germination to drown caterpillars that try to attack seedlings.
Remove cotton residues after harvest to destroy overwintering sites.
Plough in the autumn and then do shallow tillage to suppress late autumn and early spring weeds
Avoid intercropping / adjacent-cropping with host crops such as peanut or maize
Implement dry–wet crop rotation: 1st year cotton, 2nd year plant rice to drown pupa + caterpillars.
Monitoring: Caterpillars cut stems at base of young plants
Search for caterpillars near roots and on lower leaves, at seedling and young plant stage in mornings once per week
Colour of caterpillars is uniform and varies from light to dark grey but without any distinct stripes or markings, as other caterpillar species have.
If 0.5-1 caterpillars of 1 to 3rd instar (< 2 cm long) are found per m 2 consider action (1 every 4th to 5th plant)
If 1 to 2 caterpillars at 3 to 5th (> 2 cm long) are found per m 2 consider action (1 every 3rd to 4th plant)
Adult moths have a black wedge or dagger shaped black marking on its outer margin of wings.
Direct Control: Check the soil around the cut seedlings and collect cutworms
Shortly irrigate for less than 1 hour frequently because cutworms stop feeding in wet soils.
Put straw-residue stem- trap (bound dry grass stovers) in the middle of cotton field when moths fly and replace every week.
Burn to destroy the laid eggs.
Install 5 to 6 black light lamps per 667 m 2 about 1.5m from ground to trap and kill moths.
Place 5-6 self-made odour traps per 667 m 2 about 1.5m from ground.
Fill a mix of sugar, water, vinegar at ratio 6:10:3 + some drops of soap into
PET bottles/canisters with large openings at sides.
